problem_type: Public asset retrieval method and anonymous upload fallback ordering
symptom: Provider probes using HEAD receive 404 for assets that GET serves, and anonymous uploads try the known 403 host before tmpfiles.
direct_cause: The Relay fetch router only dispatched GET and read() always returned a body; ANON_UPLOAD_CHAIN registered litterbox before tmpfiles.
class_root: The shared asset channel contract did not require metadata-equivalent HEAD handling or encode the empirically preferred anonymous host order at its single registry boundary.
affected_population: Any provider or probe that checks a Nomi Relay asset with HEAD
Image, video, and audio local assets using the anonymous fallback chain
internal_only_reason: The invariant is Nomi's application-level Relay and fallback ordering contract; no dependency behavior is needed to decide it.
invariants: GET and HEAD for a live Relay asset return the same status and metadata headers, while HEAD has no body.
GET and HEAD apply the same missing and expiry checks.
ANON_UPLOAD_CHAIN tries tmpfiles before litterbox for every accepted media kind.

door_reduction.why_not: The registry and resolver are separate desktop boundaries: the registry owns declarations and the resolver owns candidate selection. The Relay worker lives outside the door-map scan roots and is covered by its own shared read boundary and tests.

generality_proof: All Relay asset reads converge on read(), and all anonymous desktop uploads resolve the single ANON_UPLOAD_CHAIN registry constant before resolveLocalAsset iterates its hosts.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own lookup, expiry, metadata, and GET/HEAD body semantics for every Relay asset read.
Own the ordered anonymous fallback host list for all accepted media kinds.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both methods dispatch to read(), which owns the shared lookup and expiry checks.
The resolver iterates the registry chain for image, video, and audio candidates.
Class regression coverage exercises live, expired, and missing HEAD cases.

recurrence.reason: HEAD is a standard retrieval method used by multiple providers, and the anonymous chain is shared by every media kind and future caller.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs ANON_UPLOAD_CHAIN -> electron/catalog/assetLocalization.ts read door
rg -n 'request.method.*GET|/v1/assets/|ANON_UPLOAD_CHAIN' workers electron tests -> Relay router, read(), and desktop resolver
Existing assetLocalization tests cover anonymous image/video/audio acceptance and host fallback behavior.

prevention.invariant: Every Relay GET/HEAD asset read shares lookup/expiry/metadata logic; every anonymous upload uses the registry's tmpfiles-first order.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown, missing, or expired keys return 404 for both methods; failed first anonymous hosts proceed to the next configured host.
prevention.strategy: Route both retrieval methods into one read boundary and encode the measured fallback order once in the shared registry.

legacy_paths.rationale: No obsolete file path remains callable; the old method guard and host order are replaced in place at their shared boundaries.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in Nomi routing and registry policy; no third-party runtime controls the invariant.

migration: No persisted data or URL format changes; existing asset keys remain readable through GET and HEAD.
residual_risks: The worker fix is locally tested but intentionally not deployed, so live Cloudflare behavior remains pending deployment verification.
The probe's external provider observations remain evidence in the research report and are not re-run as part of unit tests.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Relay read semantics are owned by read() and its fetch router; anonymous ordering is separately owned by the registry, with desktop resolver coverage in the listed class tests.
